title: verify: X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig verifier
description:
Implement verification of the X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig header using ed25519-dalek.

What: crates/verify/src/verifiers/usenet_sig.rs

Header format (from existing signing code):
  X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig: v=1; a=ed25519; t=<unix-ts>; pk=<base64-pubkey>; sig=<base64-sig>

Algorithm:
1. parse_usenet_sig_header(raw_message: &[u8]) -> Option<SigHeader>
   Scan header section (stop at blank line) for 'X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig:' (case-insensitive).
   Parse v=, a=, t=, pk=, sig= tags.
   Return None if header absent.
2. canonical_bytes(raw_message: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>
   The signed bytes are the article with the X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig header value removed but header name retained (same convention as DKIM h= signing). Check existing signing code in crates/core for exact canonicalization.
3. Decode pk= as base64 → ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey.
4. Decode sig= as base64 → ed25519_dalek::Signature.
5. key_id = sha256:<hex(pk_bytes)>.
6. verifying_key.verify(canonical_bytes, &signature) → Pass or Fail.
7. Return VerificationRecord { check_type: UsenetIpfsSig, key_id: Some(key_id), result, detail: None }.
   SeenKey { key_type: 'ed25519', key_data: pk_bytes, cert_der: None, identity: None }.

pub async fn verify_usenet_sig(raw: &[u8], store: &VerifyStore, cid: &Cid) -> VerificationRecord

Defensive rules:
- base64 decode failure → result NoKey, log debug.
- Header absent → result NoKey (not Fail; absence is not forgery).
- Never log the signature bytes or key material at INFO.
